correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite horizons the symmetric survival Bellman map preserves the cone d_j>=0 and d_{j+1}<=3d_j, including explicit center and endpoint checks. This proves a single stationary nearer-boundary policy is simultaneously tail-optimal for each stage. Stagewise conditional-quantile comparison gives global tail dominance for all history-dependent policies. Exact tridiagonal first/second-moment solutions yield the sharp \(6n-129/4\) asymptotic, while a common-excursion coupling to biased walk with exponential moments and Lyapunov yield the CLT. The delivered Python standard-library checker replayed 39,497 exact assertions; finite tests do not substitute for the infinite proof.
